headline: France orders curfews. 2,400 arrested, no one killed.
summary: France's prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, ordered "very limited" local curfews Monday after a weekend of rioting that followed nationwide protests over living costs and schools. Looters hit hundreds of shops in Paris, Lyon and Marseille. Limoges's 19th-century city hall lost its roof to fire. Police arrested 2,400. No one died.
cover_answer: Yes. Lecornu's answer is to keep them small and local.
table_question: If a few kids wreck the room, should the whole class lose recess?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: In France, across the ocean, some people got very angry this weekend, broke shop windows and lit fires in the streets. Police arrested a lot of them, and nobody died. Now some towns will have a curfew, a bedtime for the whole city. The grown-ups there have it.
5-7.why: Angry, broken windows, fires, then a bedtime for a city. Only if it comes up. A six-year-old reads your face first, so keep it flat and end on nobody died.
5-7.why_long: Cantor found a five-year-old is scared by what looks frightening, fires and broken glass, not by what it means, so the shield holds and the script keeps the pictures plain and ends on nobody died. They read your face before your words. Expect "could it happen here?" Not tonight, not on our street.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Saturday, France marched over prices and run-down schools. Some split off and hit city halls and shops; Limoges's city hall burned and lost its roof. Police arrested 2,400. Monday the prime minister ordered small, local curfews. A referee stopping play in one corner, not the whole game.
8-12.why: March, split, fire, arrests, curfew. Then the referee.
8-12.why_long: This age is building chains of cause and effect and testing whether rules land fairly, so the script runs the weekend in order and ends on a curfew that is small and local, the referee stopping play in one corner. Expect "why punish people who didn't break anything?" That is Lecornu's own argument for keeping it small.

13-17.script: Does a curfew punish everyone for a few? France's prime minister ordered "very limited" curfews Monday after 2,400 arrests. Second: the interior minister said "I am responsible for everything" and offered to quit. Macron said stay and find the failures. Is owning it enough?
13-17.why: Small curfews; a minister who owned it and stayed. Two calls.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: a curfew falls on everyone, and the man who ordered it is trying to keep it small. The script gives both, then a minister who owned the failure and stayed. Kuhn calls argument a practised skill, so let them argue the second call first. Expect "should he have quit?" I don't know is honest.

5-7.a: Prices are high and their schools are in bad shape. Most people marched. Some broke things.

8-12.a: You must be home by a set hour. Lecornu says small, and only in some places.
The minister said they lost control in some cities. He offered to quit.

13-17.a: Yes. Lecornu's answer is to keep them "very limited" and local. Enough? Your call.

13-17.q: Why did the minister try to quit?
13-17.a: He said he was responsible for all of it. Macron said no: stay and fix it.
